content.title: About
content.content: Fried bass fillet is a tender piece of freshwater fish, pan‑fried until golden and crispy. Bass has a mild, slightly sweet flavor and a firm texture, making it a popular dish in both restaurants and home kitchens.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bass belongs to the Percidae family and is widespread in rivers and lakes across Europe and North America.
In the wild, bass can change its coloration to blend with its surroundings, helping it avoid predators.
Frying preserves much of the vitamin D naturally present in the fish.
Bass is featured in traditional dishes such as Japanese "tempura bass" and Scandinavian "fried bass".
Its omega‑3 fatty acid content is higher than that of many other freshwater fish.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Omega‑3s support heart health, reduce inflammation, and promote brain function.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Easily digestible protein is essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Vitamin D source
items.content: Vitamin D is important for bone health and immune function, especially in low‑sunlight regions.

items.title: Minerals: selenium and phosphorus
items.content: Selenium acts as an antioxidant, while phosphorus is vital for energy metabolism.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with many red meat products, fried bass contains less saturated fat.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Heavy metal content
items.content: Freshwater bass can accumulate cadmium and mercury; moderate consumption is advised.

items.title: Calorie density from frying
items.content: Frying adds extra calories, so portion control is recommended.

items.title: Foodborne illness risk
items.content: Improper storage or undercooking can allow bacterial growth leading to food poisoning.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the fried bass fillet hot, often with a squeeze of lemon, fresh herbs, or a light sauce. It pairs well with mashed potatoes, vegetable sides, or salads. For a lighter option, pan‑fry in a small amount of olive oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked fried bass in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze in a sealed bag at –18 °C, where it retains quality for up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C before serving.
